To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We describe qDIET, a new tool for automated, self-sufficient linking of grocery point-of-sale data to the USDA's HEI-20005/10 nutritional content database.
the quality Dietary Information Extration Tool (qDIet) can be used to calculate the Healthy Eating Index-2005/10 from retail grocery purchase data.
we developed a new tool, qDIET, which is an automated system that can link point-of-sale grocery items to their corresponding USDA nutrient database entries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the creation of a tool to facilitate the calculation of a dietary quality metric in a manner that can be easily implemented in clinical practice.
developing a tool to assist patients and clinicians in the shared decision making process regarding effective weight loss strategies.
developing an automated process to link grocery items to their appropriate nutrient content data, so that the HEI-2010 can be calculated from retail purchase records.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

qDIET is a novel tool that is able to link point-of-sale data to the appropriate databases in the USDA to facilitate the calculation of the dietary quality metric, the HEI, and that this tool can be used as a foundation to develop a comprehensive and self-sustaining system that can link point-of-sale grocery data to the appropriate nutritional databases in the USDA.
we have developed a new tool, qDIET, to facilitate the automated calculation of the HEIs from point of sale grocery data.
qDIET can be used to link retail grocery purchase records to the appropriate USDA database to permit the calculation and monitoring of the HEI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a tool to help clinicians advise their patients on the dietary quality of the food that they buy.

we are working toward a process that would enable the creation of a national, longitudinal dietary quality database, which would be of enormous value to clinicians, patients, researchers, and public health agencies.
we have created a prototype that demonstrates the feasibility of linking point-of-sale grocery data with the HEI-2010.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we believe that the HEI- 2005/2011 is a metric with the potential to be a powerful tool for clinicians and patients to monitor dietary quality and to facilitate shared decision-making about diet and weight.

the HEI-2010 is a metric that can serve as a useful tool in shared decision-making between clinicians and patients, and that qDIET is a step toward making this metric more accessible to clinicians and their patients.
